correctness.rationale: Incidence multiplication expands \(N^h\) as sums over strict chains. In a rooted tree a length-\(h\) chain must follow the unique root-to-depth-\(h\) Hasse path, hence no cancellation; only the root row can be nonzero, giving rank 0 or 1, equal to the multiplicity of size-\(h+1\) Jordan blocks. Independent cover labels give the bottom-up recurrence. Strict ancestor pair counting yields \(M_h\); branch complement counting yields the integer recurrence. Strict concavity and a reciprocal-difference estimate give respectively the supercritical limit and critical \(4/h\) asymptotic. Direct exhaustive and random matrix-power checks on the supplied checker corroborate all critical small cases, including characteristic 2 and an extension field. Limits: no formula for smaller Jordan blocks.

originality.rationale: The exact incidence-radical top-Jordan-block count, uniqueness of that block, and the finite-field critical boundary are not statements supplied by the inspected incidence-involution, generic triangular-Jordan, or random-triangular-rank theorems. A unique-chain comparison is essential: the full-triangular results average over many paths and do not imply this tree-sparse probability law. The branching survival relation and its fixed points are classical and not asserted as new. Material read and residual priority risks are recorded below; this is a best-knowledge comparison, not uniqueness certification.

value.rationale: The maximal nilpotency index and highest Jordan block are natural invariants of a nilpotent element in the canonical representation of a finite-dimensional incidence algebra. The result supplies the complete exact counting law for this invariant on all finite rooted-tree posets, a linear-time evaluator for arbitrary branching patterns, a unique maximal-block multiplicity constraint, and an explicit finite-field critical boundary in growing full trees. These features are structurally distinct from aggregate Jordan-type totals for unrestricted triangular matrices. The classical probabilistic recurrence alone is not assigned value as an independently new fact.
